item.title: Ba qualifies for 2027 OFC Men’s Champions League
item.description: Ba FC has qualified for the 2027 OFC Men’s Champions League after winning the 2026 Extra Premier League title. The club says this is another historic achievement for Ba and credits the achievement to the hard work of the players, coaching staff and management.
item.content:encoded:
Ba FC has qualified for the 2027 OFC Men’s Champions League after winning the 2026 Extra Premier League title.

The club says this is another historic achievement for Ba and credits the achievement to the hard work of the players, coaching staff and management.

Ba FC has also thanked its fans for their continued support.

The 2027 OFC Men’s Champions League will be played in Fiji from 29th August to 11th September 2027.

Ba has also qualified for the Champion verses Champion.

The Men in Black have enjoyed a successful season, winning both the BiC Fiji FACT and the 2026 Extra Premier League titles.

item.title: ACS and Sigatoka Methodist eye Raluve final spots
item.description: Excitement is building for a thrilling weekend of 2026 Weet-Bix Raluve semi-final, with ACS chasing a place in the grand final and Sigatoka Methodist determined to replicate last year’s run and go all the way again. With only one victory standing between each team and the biggest game of the season, the pressure is on across the U16 and U18 grades.
item.content:encoded:
Excitement is building for a thrilling weekend of 2026 Weet-Bix Raluve semi-final, with ACS chasing a place in the grand final and Sigatoka Methodist determined to replicate last year’s run and go all the way again.

With only one victory standing between each team and the biggest game of the season, the pressure is on across the U16 and U18 grades.

In the U16 grade, ACS will face Nasinu in a highly anticipated semi-final on Saturday, while Sigatoka Methodist will take on St Vincent College.

ACS returns to the semi-finals after coming within minutes of reaching last year’s grand final.

T hey will be determined to finish the job this time and secure their place in the decider.

Standing in their way is a Nasinu side that has fought its way into the final four and will be looking to produce a major upset.

For Sigatoka Methodist, the semi-final represents another opportunity to replicate their 2025 run, when they reached the grand final.

T hey will be hoping their experience on the big stage can help them take another step towards a return to the decider, but St Vincent College has earned its place among the final four and will have no intention of simply making up the numbers.

The U18 grade also promises exciting contests, with MGM facing ACS and Lomary meeting Sila Central.

The times for the matches have not been confirmed.

item.title: Delta Tigers roar back with 4-2 win to keep OFC semi-final hopes alive
item.description: Rewa FC have bounced back strongly with a 4-2 victory over Solomons's Tupapa Maraerenga in their OFC Men’s Champions League campaign. Ramzan Khan opened the scoring for Rewa in the 39th minute, giving the Delta Tigers a 1-nil lead heading into halftime.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC have bounced back strongly with a 4-2 victory over Solomons's Tupapa Maraerenga in their OFC Men’s Champions League campaign.

Ramzan Khan opened the scoring for Rewa in the 39th minute, giving the Delta Tigers a 1-nil lead heading into halftime.

Rewa came out firing in the second half, with Joseph Athale finding the back of the net in the 47th minute to extend their lead.

Setareki Hughes added Rewa’s third goal in the 66th minute, with Josaia Sela scoring in the 85th minute to help secure the victory.

The win gives Rewa and their fans renewed hope as they look ahead to their next match.

They need to win their next match to qualify for the semi final.

Rewa will now turn their attention to their next match against Solomon Islands' Lae City this Saturday at 3pm at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.

item.title: Navatu Secondary flying North’s flag in Super Deans semi-finals
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/08/2026 The Navatu Secondary School Under-19 rugby team has defied the odds and will fly the flag for the Northern Division at this week’s Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans semi-finals.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/08/2026

The Navatu Secondary School Under-19 rugby team has defied the odds and will fly the flag for the Northern Division at this week’s Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans semi-finals.

Navatu Secondary is located in Cakaudrove Province on Vanua Levu and is the only team from the North to have reached the semifinals.

The team had a grand celebration as it departed Vanua Levu for Suva, bringing with it the blessings of the vanua and the people.

Navatu Secondary School has been consistent in the Under-19 division, defeating Queen Victoria School 19-12 in the national playoffs before overcoming Suva Grammar School 19-15 in the quarter-finals.

This Saturday, Navatu Secondary will face Ratu Kadavulevu School at 1.50pm at Buckhurst Park.

In the Under-18 semi-finals, Suva Grammar School will meet Ra High School at 3pm at Churchill Park in Lautoka, while Lelean Memorial School will face Nasinu Secondary School at 3.40pm at HFC Bank Stadium.
